scope: Current storage summary and counters during pending/unknown upload; no reopening of accepted persistence or control corrections
evidence_kind: Source-confirmed call flow; no runtime/UI stall reproduction

finding.title: Current-storage summary appears before any frame ACK and remains through pending/unknown upload

locations.fact: storing maps to Storing while capturing.; also used by menuLine
Successful display-source registration publishes storing then starts upload runner
Whole uploader awaited with no pending-status publication first
Unknown upload changes job outcome only; publishCounts preserves overall state
counts copies existing status, so unknown counts do not clear storing summary

finding.counter_distinction: Confirmed stored total is not optimistic: committed only after fully corresponding batch ACK. The newly journaled sending job is not immediately published, so pending/unknown count may remain stale or hidden during first await.
finding.impact: Potentially misleading current-service progress/receipt wording; not demonstrated data loss, unauthorized sends or premature stored-count increment.

smallest_owner_change: Use a neutral active-link/attempting-transfer summary that does not promise current server storage while requests may be pending; retain confirmed receipt counters.
Publish the existing sending/unknown counts before awaiting a journaled upload so a held request is visible. No new protocol or timer framework is required.
Pending, missing reply and timeout must remain unknown, never relabeled known not stored; later corresponding ACK may increment confirmed count.
bounded_followup_acceptance: Hold the first original/batch transport answer: pending count is visible and summary makes no current-storage assertion; stored remains unchanged.
Release exact receipts/ACK: only then increment confirmed stored count.
Return or exhaust unknown: retain unknown and keep neutral summary; preserve prior ACK counts.
existing_evidence: Root reports actual native78 pass for fb891d6; accepted as prior evidence, not rerun or recounted here. Windows182-second observation is Windows-only and not a measured Mac duration.
limitations: No Mac GUI hang was reproduced; actual duration and Darwin timeout behavior are unmeasured.
60-second request/300-second resource timeout defaults and bounded retries exist in source; they do not establish actual end-to-end stall timing.
